points.title: The main rule
points.must: Every data flow must start or end at a process — data is stored, read or passed on only by a process.

points.title: Why the rules exist
points.must: A DFD is a specification: an arrow promises software moves the data; an entity cannot write into a store without a program to validate it.

points.title: Allowed and not allowed flows
points.must: Allowed: entity→process, process→entity, process→store, store→process, process→process. Not allowed: entity→entity, entity↔store, store→store, each with the reason; fix by adding a process.

points.title: Rules for processes
points.must: At least one input and one output; verb + noun name; numbers only identify, they do not show order.

points.title: Rules for stores and flows
points.must: Each store written and read; may be drawn twice; plural noun; flows carry data (not goods or money), one direction per arrow, named with a noun; no decisions or loops.

points.title: Black hole, miracle and grey hole
points.must: Black hole: inputs but no output; miracle: outputs but no input; grey hole: inputs not enough for the outputs; each with an example and how to check a process.

points.title: Finding errors (worked example)
points.must: Gym example or similar: illegal flows identified with the reason and the correction.

points.title: Reading the scenario
points.must: People who give/receive data → entities; kept things → stores; verbs → processes; group verbs into 3–7 main processes.

points.title: Entity or data store?
points.must: Same word can be both (Customer vs D1 Customers); acts → entity, kept → store; the system controls its stores, not entities.

points.title: Steps to draw a level-1 DFD
points.must: Underline entities; verbs → processes; kept data → stores; list inputs/outputs of each process; draw with named arrows; check rules and balance.

points.title: Pizza shop level-1 DFD
points.must: Entities Customer, Bank, Kitchen; processes Take order, Process payment, Send order to kitchen; stores Menu, Orders; named flows.

points.title: Checking and reading back a DFD
points.must: Each process has input and output; each store written and read; no illegal flows; all flows labelled; balanced; read the diagram back sentence by sentence against the scenario.

points.title: Flowchart and ERD
points.must: Definitions: flowchart = sequence of steps, decisions and loops; ERD = entities, attributes and relationships of a database.

points.title: DFD vs flowchart vs ERD
points.must: Arrow means 'data moves' vs 'next step'; whole system vs one process vs database; how they link (process → flowchart, store → table).

points.title: Advantages and limitations
points.must: Advantages: simple, client can check, whole system on one page, finds missing data; limitations: no order, no algorithms, many levels for big systems.
